data.name: SetupHeader
data.value: Set up this PC for the remote

data.name: SetupIntro
data.value: So that the phone can control VLC, the companion needs a few permissions and settings on this PC. Here is what each of them does and why it is needed. Nothing changes until you press Apply.

data.name: SetupFooterNote
data.value: You can open this window at any time from the tray icon menu: “Setup and permissions…”.

data.name: SetupFirewallText
data.value: The phone connects to this PC over Wi‑Fi, and Windows blocks incoming connections until you allow them. The companion will allow itself and VLC to accept connections on private (home) networks only. Windows will ask for administrator permission once.

data.name: SetupFirewallOff
data.value: ✓ Windows Firewall is off for private networks: nothing to allow

data.name: SetupFirewallMissing
data.value: Not allowed yet: Windows will block the phone

data.name: SetupFirewallBlocked
data.value: ⚠ A firewall rule blocks {0} (usually left by “Cancel” in a Windows prompt). Apply removes it.

data.name: SetupFirewallUnknown
data.value: Could not read the firewall rules: {0}

data.name: SetupFirewallWaiting
data.value: Waiting for administrator permission: confirm the Windows prompt…

data.name: SetupFirewallCancelled
data.value: ⚠ Administrator permission was not given. Press Apply to try again, or allow access when Windows asks.

data.name: SetupFirewallFailed
data.value: ✗ Could not change the firewall rules ({0}). Details are in the log.

data.name: SetupFirewallNotManaged
data.value: Not managed by the companion: allow access yourself when Windows asks

data.name: SetupPublicNetwork
data.value: ⚠ The network “{0}” is public. Windows does not let the phone in on public networks: make it private in the network settings.

data.name: SetupAutostartText
data.value: The companion starts when you sign in to Windows, so the phone can control VLC without anyone touching the PC. It uses your own startup list; no administrator rights are needed.

data.name: SetupVlcText
data.value: VLC gets its web interface turned on with a password made by the companion, so VLC opened in any way (even by a double-click on a movie) can be controlled from the phone. The companion edits VLC's settings file (a backup copy is kept) and installs helper pages for audio tracks and subtitles. VLC's own “continue playback?” question is turned off: the phone asks instead.

data.name: SetupVlcRunning
data.value: VLC is running: its settings will be written after it closes

data.name: SetupVlcNotInstalled
data.value: VLC is not installed. Install VLC 3.x, then open this window again from the tray menu.

data.name: SetupVlcOff
data.value: Off: VLC's settings stay as they are

data.name: SetupVlcFailed
data.value: ✗ Could not configure VLC (details are in the log)

data.name: SetupKeepAwakeTitle
data.value: Keep the PC awake during a movie

data.name: SetupKeepAwakeText
data.value: While a movie is playing, Windows won't put the PC to sleep or turn off the screen. When playback stops, your usual power settings apply again.

data.name: SetupMediaText
data.value: Folders with your movies and series, on this PC's disks or network shares. The companion recognizes the titles by the file names and fetches posters and descriptions, and the phone shows them as a library. Other folders can still be opened from the drives.

data.name: SetupMediaPick
data.value: Choose a folder with movies or series

data.name: SetupMediaNone
data.value: No folders yet: the phone browses the drives only

data.name: SetupMediaTmdb
data.value: Posters and descriptions: TMDB. This product uses the TMDB API but is not endorsed or certified by TMDB.

data.name: SetupMediaStationTitle
data.value: This PC is a media station

data.name: SetupMediaStationText
data.value: For a PC or laptop that lives at the TV: it keeps working with the lid closed and never goes to sleep or hibernates by itself — plugged in and on battery, so a power cut does not stop it either. The companion changes these settings of the current Windows power plan; unticking this later does not change them back. The screen may still turn off, and the TV may go to standby.

data.name: SetupMediaStationOk
data.value: ✓ The lid can be closed; the PC does not go to sleep

data.name: SetupMediaStationOff
data.value: Off: the usual Windows power settings apply

data.name: BalloonMediaStationDrift
